title: CLO Tips Workshop - Making Elastic Drawstrings
description: You can purchase items using the CONNECT mall to create elastic drawstring decorations on down jackets! Simple and practical, learn it in 6 minutes!
transcript:
Hello everyone,  
I will show you how to make a spring-loaded plate.  
I have already converted the eye part of the face into a hole.  
Next, click on the 3D window and find the plate.  
Use the lift tool to create a spring-loaded plate.  
Draw two inner lines at the front of the eye.  
The length of the inner line is the same as the width of the spring-loaded plate.  
It is 1.5.  
After drawing, you can see its position in the 3D window.  
Since the plate is in a moving state,  
the inner line is symmetrical.  
Next,  
sew the spring-loaded plate to the inner plate.  
Now, choose the spring-loaded plate in the 2D window.  
Use the quick arrangement tool next to the positioning ball in the 3D window.  
Arrange the plate near the eye.  
To increase the simulation speed,  
you can use your sending Julia to check its position.  
Then, adjust the position of the center position to the three-das,  
and then,  
press the Allen button to change the position.  
After the simulation time,  
let's explore creating a spring-loaded plate.  
You can use the Edit Selection Tool to change the selection line and simulate it again.  
The other side is also the same operation.  
After the adjustment is complete, we will adjust the shape again.  
Now the board is a C-shape.  
Next, use the fixed needle tool.  
Add two fixed needles to the drawstring board.  
Use the Selection Tool to adjust its position.  
Adjust the board to the shape of a pass-through adjustment buckle.  
You can also further reduce the strength of the drawstring board.  
Next, we will adjust the shape of the drawstring board.  
The fixed needle can be added in the 3D window, and the same can be added in the 2D window.  
Continue to adjust its shape.  
After the adjustment is almost done, we enter the Connect layer in the drawstring window.  
Add the adjusted buckle that has been added in advance.  
Select Add to workspace with six keys.  
Select Open and use the glue tool to directly stick it on the drawboard,  
adjust the size, and then use the positioning tool to adjust its position.  
In addition, in the 3D window, you can directly adjust the size of the component,  
select this component in the object window,  
and in the attribute editor, you can accurately modify the size of the component.  
Now let's continue to adjust the position of the component.  
Insert the drawboard into the adjustment button.  
After the adjustment is complete, we can start the simulation.  
Since the component has already been pasted onto the drawboard,  
the component is more visible.  
This is done according to the simulation of the drawboard.  
Now let's adjust its details.  
After the adjustment is complete,  
we will add a rendering thickness to the drawboard.  
Now the horizontal drawstring is finished.  
Now directly Ctrl D will align the finished board and copy it.  
Similarly, the two boards of the hat will be frozen,  
and the previously made drawstring will be frozen.  
Let's simulate the parallel drawstring.  
After the adjustment is complete,  
we can adjust the position of the component.  
After the adjustment is complete,  
we will freeze the drawstring board.  
Now the parallel drawstring on both sides  
is completed.  
Finally, let's add the eye of the eye.  
Use the twist tool to add the eye of the eye.  
We need to pay attention to this.  
We need to turn off the twist of the twist.  
Then use the positioning tool to adjust the position of the eye of the eye.  
After the adjustment is complete,  
we will copy the twist to the board of the symmetrical adjustment.  
Similarly, we need to adjust its position on the other side.  
Finally, we will activate all the boards.  
Our spring-loaded drawstring is now complete.  
Let's have a look at the final results.  
See you in the next video.  
Good luck!

chunks.content: ## Making a Spring-Loaded Plate in CLO This section explains how to create a spring-loaded plate in CLO, focusing on using the lift tool, drawing precise inner lines, and arranging components in both 2D and 3D windows for accurate simulation. 1. Convert the eye part of the face into a hole. 2. In the 3D window, locate the plate. 3. Use the **Lift Tool** to create the spring-loaded plate. 4. Draw two inner lines at the front of the eye in the 2D window. The length of these lines should equal the width of the spring-loaded plate, which is 1.5 units. 5. The inner lines are symmetrical since the plate is in a moving state. 6. Sew the spring-loaded plate to the inner plate. 7. Select the spring-loaded plate in the 2D window, then use the **Quick Arrangement Tool** near the positioning ball in the 3D window to position the plate near the eye. 8. To increase simulation speed, use the *Sending Julia* function to check the position. 9. Adjust the center position in the 3D window and press the **Align (Allen) Button** to change the position accordingly. 10. Use the **Edit Selection Tool** to modify the selection line and re-simulate as needed. 11. Repeat the same process for the opposite side. --- ## Shaping and Securing the Drawstring Board This section details adjusting the drawstring board’s shape, adding fixed needles, and modeling it to fit a pass-through adjustment buckle, including fine-tuning its strength and dimensions. 1. After initial adjustments, the board takes a C-shape. 2. Use the **Fixed Needle Tool** to add two fixed needles to the drawstring board. 3. Adjust needle positions with the **Selection Tool**. 4. Shape the board to fit the pass-through adjustment buckle. 5. Reduce the drawstring board’s strength if necessary for better simulation. 6. Fixed needles can be added and adjusted in both the 3D and 2D windows. 7. Continue refining the board’s shape until the desired form is achieved. --- ## Attaching the Buckle and Component Size Adjustment This section covers adding the buckle to the drawstring board using the Connect layer and glue tool, as well as precise size and position modifications using the attribute editor and positioning tools. 1. Enter the **Connect Layer** in the drawstring window. 2. Add the pre-adjusted buckle to the workspace using six keys. 3. Select **Open** and use the **Glue Tool** to attach the buckle directly onto the drawboard. 4. Adjust the buckle’s size and position with the **Positioning Tool**. 5. In the 3D window, select the buckle component in the Object window. 6. Use the **Attribute Editor** to modify component size accurately. 7. Insert the drawboard into the adjustment button for final positioning. 8. Once positioned, start the simulation to verify component visibility and behavior. --- ## Finalizing the Drawstring Assembly and Simulation This section describes adding rendering thickness, duplicating components, freezing boards, and simulating parallel drawstrings for both sides of the hat. 1. Add rendering thickness to the drawboard to complete the horizontal drawstring.

chunks.content: In the 3D window, select the buckle component in the Object window. 6. Use the **Attribute Editor** to modify component size accurately. 7. Insert the drawboard into the adjustment button for final positioning. 8. Once positioned, start the simulation to verify component visibility and behavior. --- ## Finalizing the Drawstring Assembly and Simulation This section describes adding rendering thickness, duplicating components, freezing boards, and simulating parallel drawstrings for both sides of the hat. 1. Add rendering thickness to the drawboard to complete the horizontal drawstring. 2. Use **Ctrl + D** to align and duplicate the finished board. 3. Freeze the two hat boards and the previously created drawstring to stabilize the simulation. 4. Simulate the parallel drawstring on both sides. 5. Adjust component positions as needed. 6. Freeze the drawstring boards after final adjustments. 7. Parallel drawstrings on both sides are now complete. --- ## Adding and Adjusting the Eyelet (Eye of the Eye) This section explains how to add the eyelet using the twist tool, disable unwanted twisting effects, position the eyelet properly, and duplicate it symmetrically. 1. Use the **Twist Tool** to add the eyelet ("eye of the eye"). 2. Disable the twist effect on the twist tool to prevent deformation. 3. Use the **Positioning Tool** to place the eyelet accurately. 4. Copy the twist effect to the symmetrical adjustment board. 5. Adjust the eyelet’s position on the opposite side. 6. Activate all boards to finalize the spring-loaded drawstring assembly. --- ## Summary of Completed Spring-Loaded Drawstring The spring-loaded drawstring assembly, including the spring-loaded plate, drawstring board with fixed needles, buckle attachment, parallel drawstring simulation, and eyelet adjustments, is now complete and ready for further use or rendering in CLO.
